pr.title: Keep clean on a head a review signed off after the push that queued the label workflow
pr.head: 24aa643c620ddf9ba7bcfcf69a26957da7f54c82

summary: Projector marks a pull request whose current head a review signed off with the clean label. In a repository that requires the projector/review commit status, project init also writes a GitHub Actions workflow, .github/workflows/projector-clean.yml, that takes clean off whenever a commit is pushed, because a new head has no review yet.

That workflow decided whether to run from the labels the push event recorded, then removed the label from the pull request as it was when the job ran. A job that ran late, such as one stuck in a queue or re-run later, which replays the old event, could remove clean from a head that a review signed off after the push. Nothing put the label back, because Projector decides sign-off from the review verdicts, so the head never got another review.
The workflow's step now reads the pull request when it runs:

1. The label is already gone. The step exits and changes nothing.
  2. The current head has a success projector/review status. A review signed that head off, so the step keeps the label.
  3. Anything else. The step removes the label. It then reads the head and its status again, and gives the label back when a review signed the head off in the meantime. After giving it back, it reads the head once more and takes the label off again when a push moved the head.

publish, which adds clean, now reads the head again right after it adds the label, and takes the label back off when a push moved the head during the edit. Such a push records no clean in its event, so the workflow would skip it.

init recognizes the workflow 0.8.14 wrote by its SHA-256 digest and replaces it, reporting updated, and still keeps a file someone edited. For a kept copy it points at the new project review workflow, which prints the current workflow to compare with. upgrade now says when a release changes the clean workflow.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first Projector review, of b8dabd2, was clean and suggested closing a gap in publish. The next head closed it.
  • The review of b1f984b asked to rewrap two docs/cli.md paragraphs, and suggested a re-read after the step gives the label back and a step test for a moving head.
  • 24aa643 does all three, and its review is clean, with no finding thread open.
  • The full test suite, project check, and git diff --check pass at 24aa643.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Signed off. The newest Projector verdict on the head is clean and no finding thread is open.
  • projector/review. The commit status publish posts on the reviewed commit, success when signed off, wherever the default branch requires it.
  • Event labels. The labels GitHub records in a pull_request_target event at the moment of the push. A re-run replays them unchanged.

groups.title: The workflow and publish read the pull request when they act
groups.kicker: Where clean is taken off, kept, or given back
intro: The template is the file init renders into each repository. Its job still starts only when the push event listed clean, so a push to a pull request without the label starts no runner. The step reads the pull request's head and labels, then that head's combined commit status, and removes the label only when no review signed the head off. After removing it, the step reads the head and status once more, so a review that landed between the first read and the removal keeps its label. After giving the label back, it reads the head a third time, because a push that landed meanwhile recorded no label in its event and its job skips.

publish is the only command that adds clean. After adding it, publish reads the pull request again and takes the label off if the head moved. A push before that read recorded no label in its event, so only this read can catch it. A push after it records the label, and that push's workflow job takes it off.

files.note: The rendered workflow: reads the head and status, removes the label, gives it back to a head signed off meanwhile, and takes it off again when the head moved.

checks.text: This if still reads the event's labels, so a push that records no clean starts no job. publish's re-read and the step's third head read cover the cases where that matters.

The review walked a push landing before and after each read and edit of the step. Each order ends with clean on a head only when a review signed that head off, apart from a failing gh call, which fails the step visibly.

groups.title: init replaces the earlier release's workflow
groups.kicker: How an existing repository gets the new step
intro: write_clean_workflow runs inside init only after it finds or creates the ruleset that requires projector/review. A file equal to the template is unchanged. A file whose digest matches a workflow an earlier release wrote is replaced and reported updated. Any other file is kept, and init says how to compare it with project review workflow. The new subcommand is added to Projector's Codex permission rules.

files.note: Replaces an earlier release's workflow, adds project review workflow, and adds the clean workflow to upgrade's digests.
Lets Codex run project review workflow without asking.

groups.title: Tests and documentation
groups.kicker: The step run under bash, and the init upgrade
intro: CleanWorkflowStepTests cuts the step's script out of the rendered template and runs it with bash -e, as GitHub does, against a stub gh that answers through the real jq. The stub gives each read in turn its own answer, so a test can return no status first and success second, or a different head on each read of the pull request. tests/test_review.py moves the head right after publish's label edit.

checks.text: In scratch copies, each of these mutations turned a test red: disabling the success branch, dropping case folding, changing the digest, disabling publish's re-read, making the step reuse the first head's SHA, and skipping the step's third head read.
